tool_input.description: Update renderer tests for the 90-position status region

result:
Implementation complete. `CLAUDE_ACCENT_REPORT.md` is written.

## Deployment status first

I read the rollback notice before doing anything, and it invalidated my previous report's deployment section. **This is a preview build; a restart activates nothing.** The live host is the original file and doesn't import `light_studio`. I corrected the stale claims in `CLAUDE_BUILD_REPORT.md` (marked superseded, original kept in a collapsed block), `README.md` (status banner replacing the dead Tailscale URL, plus a "what a trial would involve" section), `AGENTS.md` and `DESIGN.md`.

The renderer Adi saw was Codex's provisional build, not mine — but that doesn't make mine approved. Its smoothness on real ropes is unverified, and I've made that the gating item rather than a footnote.

## The accent zone

The structural decision that makes the guarantee hold: **`render_rope` now returns 90 pixels and has no concept of positions 90–99.** The cap is rendered separately and joined only at the end by `compose_rope`. No state, event, ripple, celebration or Identify can reach the cap because the status layer cannot address it — enforced by structure, not by a rule someone must remember. `reverse` is applied inside `compose_rope` to the status list alone, so the cap's location is a property of the geometry, not of a boolean.

Per rope: white (default) / solid colour / rainbow, own brightness, apply-to-all in two places, persisted at schema 3 with migration from schema 1/2 that preserves mapping, names, direction, settings and undo.

Two judgement calls I'd flag: **quiet mode still dims the caps to 45%** (a "quiet" wall with seventy full-white LEDs isn't quiet — one constant if you disagree), and **rainbow is uniform, not a spatial gradient** — one contiguous run means one message, stepped 72×/24 s and deliberately not tied to the speed slider so no UI control can multiply its cost.

## The two flagged issues — both confirmed real

The droplet bug was worse than described: with 90 positions an empty bucket needs ~2.97 s of falling against a fixed 2 s cycle, so below ~40% progress the drop reset in mid-air and never splashed. `observed_complete` could indeed show an old completion age against a different retained job; it now carries the job name, is retired by any unwatched interval, and I **stopped persisting it entirely** — a restart is by definition an unwatched interval, so a persisted value could never be trusted.

## Test evidence

`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` → **253 tests, OK** (192 → 253), the only command I ran.

I verified both bug fixes by **reverting them and confirming the new tests fail** (`2.0 not >= 2.027`; "no splash reached the waterline at 0%"; the job-binding assertion), then restored them.

## Unverified

No browser and no hardware here — UI behaviour is statically checked, not executed. Also worth checking on one rope before trusting all seven: the assumption that physical position 0 is the data-in wire. If a rope is wired the other way its cap will appear at the wire end, and that's a per-rope fact, not a global one.
